items.label: text
items.text: bulb a glass object that produces light when electricity is passed through it. Or, the wider part of some plastic pipettes, which is squeezed to allow the pipette to be filled condensation polymerisation polymerisation of monomers in which each time two monomers combine, a small molecule such as water or hydrogen chloride is removed

items.label: text
items.text: calorimetry measuring the heat given out or taken in by a chemical reaction

items.label: text
items.text: carboxylic acids a homologous series of compounds which all contain a -COOH functional group attached to a hydrocarbon chain

items.label: text
items.text: catalyst substance that speeds up a chemical reaction by providing an alternative pathway of lower activation energy. Catalysts are not used up and remain chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction

items.label: text
items.text: catalytic converter a device used in cars to convert oxides of nitrogen and carbon monoxide into harmless nitrogen gas and carbon dioxide. It uses platinum, palladium and rhodium as catalysts

items.label: text
items.text: cathode the negative electrode in electrolysis, which attracts positive cations

items.label: text
items.text: cation a positive ion, formed by atoms losing electrons

items.label: text
items.text: chemical means methods which involve chemical reactions

items.label: text
items.text: chromatogram the adsorbent paper from paper chromatography showing the separation of different coloured substances condensation reaction a chemical reaction in which two molecules combine to form a larger molecule with elimination of a small molecule such as water corrosive a substance which can damage living tissue covalent bonding strong electrostatic force of attraction between the nuclei of the atoms making up the bond and the shared pair of electrons cracking a process in which long-chain alkanes are converted to alkenes and shorter-chain alkanes. It is carried out using silica or alumina as catalyst at a temperature of 600-700°C

items.label: text
items.text: crude oil formed from the remains of living organisms when their soft tissue was gradually changed by high temperatures and pressures into a thick, black oil. It is a mixture of hydrocarbons

items.label: text
items.text: crystallisation a process in which a solute (soluble solid) is obtained from its solvent

items.label: text
items.text: damp slightly wet

items.label: text
items.text: decomposition reaction a chemical reaction in which a compound is broken down into its elements or simpler compounds

items.label: text
items.text: clump a small group or cluster dehydration removal of water

items.label: text
items.text: coefficientnumber written in front of formulae in a balanced chemical equation

items.label: text
items.text: coil continuous series of circular rings into which something such as wire or rope has been wound or twisted

items.label: text
items.text: collision theorystates that for a reaction to occur, the reactant particles must collide with each other and the collision needs to have sufficient energy and the correct orientation

items.label: text
items.text: combustion a chemical reaction in which a substance reacts with oxygen (burns) to form products and heat delocalised electrons electrons that are no longer attached to particular atoms or pairs of atoms, but are free to move throughout the whole structure denatured the loss of function of enzymes due to structural changes, usually caused by changes in temperature or pH

items.label: text
items.text: dependent variable what you measure in an experiment

items.label: text
items.text: deposition the change of state directly from a gas to a solid

items.label: text
items.text: competition reaction displacement reaction between a more reactive metal and the oxide of a less reactive metal

items.label: text
items.text: complete combustion occurs when a hydrocarbon burns in sufficient oxygen (burns) and forms carbon dioxide and water as products

items.label: text
items.text: compound a substance that forms when two or more elements chemically combine The elements cannot be separated by physical means

items.label: text
items.text: condensation the change of state from a gas to a liquid. It occurs at the condensation point diatomic a molecule that contains two atoms diffusion the random movement of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration dimerise forming a dimer - two identical molecules react to form a larger molecule dip put something into a liquid and lift out again dischargedwhen an ion loses its charge by losing or gaining electrons
